_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: When a child of the dialog uses autoFocus, focus does not return to the element that opened the dialog after it closes.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Combobox drops consumer handlers: `{...rest}` is spread before `onKeyDown={onKeyDown}` and `onBlur={onBlur}`, so consumer versions never run. Repro (C1): `onKeyDown` and `onBlur` spies got 0 calls, `onFocus` got 1.
- [blocking] Combobox selects an option that became disabled while active: ArrowDown activates "x", a rerender sets `x` to `disabled: true`, then Enter calls `onChange("x")`. The `active` lookup in `visible.find` doesn't exclude disabled options. Violates "can't be selected by key."
- [blocking] Tabs: a consumer `onKeyDown` on `<TabList>` is dropped because it is spread before the component's own `onKeyDown`. Repro (T1): spy not called on ArrowRight.
- [blocking] Tabs: `encodeURIComponent` throws on a lone surrogate, so a tab or panel with value `"a\uD800"` crashes render. Repro (T2): `URIError: URI malformed`.
- [blocking] Dialog focus trap escapes: a `tabIndex={-1}` span as the last child, clicked then Tab, puts focus on `<body>`. Repro (D2): `AFTER_TAB_FROM_SPAN <body>`, outside the dialog.
- [blocking] Dialog focus trap targets hidden elements: `TABBABLE_SELECTOR` matches `[tabindex]` and the hidden TabPanel has `tabIndex={0}`. Repro (D1): Tabs with a second panel inside a Dialog, Shift+Tab from the first tab landed on `<button>hiddenbtn</button>` (inside a `hidden` panel). In a browser, `display:none` content can't take focus, so the trap breaks.
- [minor] Dialog Escape does nothing when a nested component calls `stopPropagation` on keydown (D13 failed). The README documents only `preventDefault`. Not reproduced as a spec violation; a doc gap.
- [minor] Combobox opens only on typing or arrows, not on click. Not in the criteria; not reproduced as a bug.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog backdrop: press starts on the backdrop, mouseup lands inside the panel, and the browser fires click on the common ancestor (overlay). `onOverlayClick` then calls `onOpenChange(false)`. Repro: `fireEvent.mouseDown(overlay); fireEvent.mouseUp(screen.getByText("A")); fireEvent.click(overlay);` gives "expected spy to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times". Text selection dragged out of the panel closes the modal. The criteria only name the inside-start and backdrop-start cases, so this direction is a judgment call; I am treating it as a correctness bug.
- [minor] Combobox ArrowDown after the active option is disabled (reproduced): options Apple, Banana, Cherry; active is Banana; Banana becomes disabled; ArrowDown activates Apple, not Cherry. `nextActive` falls back to `enabled[0]` when the current value isn't in the enabled list. README says "moves to the next enabled one".
- [minor] Combobox "No results" renders only while the popup is open. With `options={[]}`, focusing the input shows nothing until the user types or presses ArrowDown. Not reproduced as a failure; judgment call against the criterion.
- [minor] Dialog trap ignores CSS `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`, only `[hidden]`/`[inert]`. Not reproduced: jsdom has no layout, so I could not drive this in a test.
- [minor] Tab `onClick` runs the consumer handler first but does not honor `preventDefault`, unlike the keyboard chaining. Reproduced that selection still happens. Not a README claim, so just inconsistent.

Earlier findings, re-verified:
- Combobox consumer onKeyDown/onBlur dropped: fixed (consumer onBlur fires; consumer preventDefault skips ArrowDown).
- Disabled-while-active selectable via Enter: fixed (Enter after disable does nothing).
- TabList consumer onKeyDown dropped: fixed (consumer runs first; preventDefault skips arrows).
- Lone surrogate "a\uD800" crashed Tabs: fixed (ids and render succeed).
- Dialog trap escaped from tabIndex=-1 span at end: fixed (Tab wraps to first).
- Dialog trap targeted hidden TabPanel elements: fixed.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix reproduced review findings in the Tabs/Dialog/Combobox components in /tmp/ff-eval-mhfr6xmr/workspace, adding a regression test for each in the component's existing test file.

FILES: src/Tabs/Tabs.tsx, src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx, src/Combobox/Combobox.tsx, their *.test.tsx, README.md.

CONSTRAINTS: No new dependencies. Keep public props unchanged. Keep changes scoped to these fixes. Update README where behavior it describes changes.

Fixes:
1. Combobox: consumer `onKeyDown` and `onBlur` (from `...rest`) are dropped. Chain them: call the consumer's handler first, then the component's; if the consumer's handler called `event.preventDefault()` on keydown, skip the component's key handling. Update README to say this (remove any line saying they're overwritten).
2. Combobox: an option that becomes disabled while active can still be selected with Enter. `active` must never be a disabled option (exclude disabled in the `active` lookup), and `choose` should refuse disabled options.
3. TabList: consumer `onKeyDown` is dropped. Chain it the same way (consumer first; skip ours if it preventDefaulted).
4. Tabs: `encodeURIComponent` throws URIError on lone surrogates (value "a\uD800" crashes render). Replace id encoding with one that never throws and stays injective and id-safe, e.g. map each UTF-16 code unit to its hex (`Array.from({length:v.length},(_,i)=>v.charCodeAt(i).toString(16)).join("-")`) or similar.
5. Dialog focus trap: (a) focus escapes to <body> when the focused element is a tabIndex=-1 element inside the panel that is the last thing in DOM order (e.g. click a `<span tabIndex={-1}>` placed after the last button, then Tab). Fix: when Tab is pressed and the active element is not one of the tabbables, compute next/previous tabbable by DOM position relative to the active element (use compareDocumentPosition), wrapping; or simply always preventDefault and move focus manually to the next/previous tabbable in the list with wrapping. (b) the tabbable list includes elements inside `hidden` ancestors (e.g. a hidden TabPanel with tabIndex=0 and buttons in it). Exclude elements that have a `[hidden]` ancestor (`el.closest('[hidden]')`), and also elements inside `inert` ancestors. Add tests: Tabs inside a Dialog with a hidden second panel — Shift+Tab from the first focusable wraps to the last *visible* tabbable; tabIndex=-1 span as last child focused then Tab goes to first tabbable.
6. Combobox: give the "No results" message `role="status"` (or aria-live="polite") so it's announced; keep its text exactly "No results".
7. Dialog README: note that Escape is handled on document keydown and is skipped if a nested handler calls preventDefault (a nested stopPropagation on a React handler does not stop it — verify what actually happens and document truthfully).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- src/index.ts exports Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Dialog, Combobox and their prop types (TabsProps, TabListProps, TabProps, TabPanelProps, DialogProps, ComboboxProps, ComboboxOption).
- Tabs: `<Tabs defaultValue? value? onValueChange?>` with `<TabList aria-label>` (role=tablist), `<Tab value disabled?>` (role=tab, aria-selected, aria-controls -> its panel id, aria-disabled/disabled when disabled), `<TabPanel value>` (role=tabpanel, aria-labelledby -> its tab id, tabIndex=0, hidden when not selected).
  - Uncontrolled with defaultValue; controlled with value — in controlled mode, clicking or arrowing calls onValueChange but the selection only changes when the parent updates value (focus may move, aria-selected doesn't). onValueChange fires in both modes.
  - With no defaultValue/value, the first non-disabled tab is selected.
  - ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move focus to next/previous tab, wrapping at the ends, skipping disabled tabs; Home/End jump to the first/last non-disabled tab. Selection follows focus (activating the focused tab). Keys other than these do nothing and don't preventDefault.
  - Roving tabindex: only the selected tab has tabIndex=0, others -1. Tab key from the selected tab goes to the panel.
  - Clicking a disabled tab does nothing.
  - Hostile: all tabs disabled except one (arrows stay on it, no infinite loop); all tabs disabled (no crash, no infinite loop); tabs added/removed dynamically (order follows DOM order); two Tabs instances on one page (ids unique, keyboard in one doesn't affect the other); a value containing spaces or special characters (ids still valid — don't embed raw value in id, or sanitize it).
- Dialog: `<Dialog open onOpenChange title description?>children</Dialog>` rendered via createPortal into document.body only when open.
  - role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby -> rendered title element id, aria-describedby -> description element id only when description given (absent otherwise).
  - On open, focus moves to the first focusable element inside the dialog; if none, to the dialog element itself (tabIndex=-1).
  - Focus trap: Tab from the last focusable wraps to the first, Shift+Tab from the first wraps to the last; with zero focusable children Tab keeps focus on the dialog. Disabled and tabindex=-1 elements are not counted as tabbable.
  - Escape calls onOpenChange(false). Clicking the backdrop (outside the dialog panel) calls onOpenChange(false); clicking/mousedown inside the panel does not, and a click that starts inside and ends on the backdrop doesn't close it.
  - When it closes (open becomes false, or unmounts while open), focus returns to the element that had focus before it opened (if still in the document).
  - Hostile: open initially true on mount (focus still moves in); Escape inside a nested element; title as a ReactNode; two dialogs' ids don't collide.
- Combobox: `<Combobox label options value onChange placeholder?>`, options `{ value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean }`, value: string | null, onChange(value: string | null). Controlled value.
  - A visible <label> associated to an <input role="combobox"> with aria-expanded, aria-controls -> listbox id, aria-autocomplete="list", aria-activedescendant -> active option id (absent when none). Listbox role=listbox with aria-labelledby the label; options role=option with aria-selected (true for the current value) and aria-disabled for disabled ones.
  - The input shows the selected option's label when not being edited; typing opens the popup and filters options by case-insensitive substring match on label.
  - ArrowDown opens the popup if closed; ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option skipping disabled ones (pick wrap or clamp, document it). Enter selects the active option (onChange(option.value)), closes the popup, and the input shows its label. Enter with no active option does nothing (does not submit a surrounding form only when the popup is open).
  - Clicking an enabled option selects it; clicking a disabled option does nothing. Click on option must not lose the selection due to input blur (use mousedown preventDefault or similar).
  - Escape closes the popup without calling onChange and restores the input text to the selected option's label (or empty).
  - When filter matches nothing, the popup shows a "No results" message (not role=option), and aria-activedescendant is absent.
  - Clearing the input text and leaving / pressing Enter with empty text: document what happens; recommended: clearing text and blurring calls onChange(null).
  - Blur closes the popup.
  - When the parent changes value externally, the input text updates to the new label.
  - Hostile: all options disabled (arrows don't loop forever, no active); filter text with regex chars like "(" or "." (must not throw / must be literal); option values that are not valid ids (spaces); value not in options (input shows empty, no crash); empty options array (shows "No results"); active option resets when the filter changes so it's never a hidden/filtered-out option.
- Tests in src/<Name>/<Name>.test.tsx cover each keyboard interaction and hostile case above, using @testing-library/user-event.
- README.md documents install/usage, each component's props (table) and keyboard behavior (table), and how to run tests/typecheck.
- `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass.

CHECKS: while working `pnpm vitest run src/Tabs src/Dialog src/Combobox`; at the end `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck`, both must pass.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 2 (sent after review 2) ===
GOAL: Fix two review findings in /tmp/ff-eval-mhfr6xmr/workspace with a regression test each.

FILES: src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx (+ Dialog.test.tsx), src/Combobox/Combobox.tsx (+ Combobox.test.tsx), README.md.

CONSTRAINTS: No new deps, no public prop changes, keep scope to these two fixes.

1. Dialog backdrop: a press that starts on the backdrop and is released inside the panel still closes the dialog (browsers fire click on the common ancestor, the overlay, so target === currentTarget). Repro: `fireEvent.mouseDown(overlay); fireEvent.mouseUp(screen.getByText("A")); fireEvent.click(overlay);` → onOpenChange called. Fix: dismiss only when both mousedown and mouseup targets were the overlay itself (track mouseup target too, e.g. onMouseUp on the overlay), and the click target is the overlay. Keep existing cases working (plain backdrop click closes; press inside then release on backdrop doesn't). Update README line "A backdrop click dismisses only when the press started and ended on the backdrop." only if needed.
2. Combobox: when the active option becomes disabled, ArrowDown jumps to the first enabled option rather than the next one after it. Make ArrowDown/ArrowUp step by position in the visible list: from the current active option's index in `visible` (even if it's now disabled), move to the next/previous enabled option, wrapping; with no active option, ArrowDown picks the first enabled and ArrowUp the last enabled. All-disabled must still return null without looping forever. One helper with a direction parameter `(visible, current, step: 1 | -1)` is fine here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Dialog: Escape calls onOpenChange(false). Clicking the backdrop (outside the dialog panel) calls onOpenChange(false); clicking/mousedown inside the panel does not, and a click that starts inside and ends on the backdrop doesn't close it.
- Combobox: ArrowDown opens the popup if closed; ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the active option skipping disabled ones (pick wrap or clamp, document it).
- Hostile: all options disabled (arrows don't loop forever, no active).
- Tests in src/<Name>/<Name>.test.tsx cover each keyboard interaction and hostile case above, using @testing-library/user-event.
- README.md documents install/usage, each component's props (table) and keyboard behavior (table), and how to run tests/typecheck.
